title: Statistics: Scatter Plots, Regression and Correlation
seo_title: Grade 12 Regression and Correlation Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Represent bivariate numerical data as a scatter plot and suggest intuitively and by simple investigation whether a linear, quadratic or exponential function would best fit the data; use a calculator to calculate the linear regression line which best fits a given set of bivariate numerical data; use a calculator to calculate the correlation co-efficient of a set of bivariate numerical data and make relevant deductions.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 12 statistics worksheets: scatter plots, the least squares regression line, predictions and the correlation coefficient. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A scatter plot shows bivariate data: look for a linear, quadratic or exponential trend.
  • The least squares regression line is ŷ = a + bx; use a calculator to find a and b.
  • Use the line to predict y for a given x (best inside the range of the data).
  • The correlation coefficient r is between −1 and 1; close to ±1 means a strong linear relationship.

Examples

Example

ŷ = 12,5 + 2,4x at x = 10

12,5 + 24

Answer: 36,5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
a and bb is the gradient; a is the intercept.
r as a %r = 0,9 is strong, not 90%.
CauseCorrelation does not prove cause.
